findings.label: Non-::4 shapes are launch/host-bound: device work is 1.4-7.7us against 66.8-133.3us eval walltime
findings.backend_detail: Ascend msprof op_summary: per-op 'Task Duration(us)' averaged over 100 invocations; 'Task Wait Time(us)' is the gap between the preceding task end and this task start. Eval latencies are taken from the authoritative eval context, not from msprof timing.

findings.inference: Authoritative eval latencies for these three workloads are 0.13328ms (float16 shape0), 0.06680ms (float16 shape2) and 0.06840ms (float16 shape3), while the profiler measures the device kernel at 1.423us, 2.612us and 7.695us respectively: the kernel occupies only 1-11% of the walltime, and the execution timeline shows launches spaced ~92-109us apart with the device idle in between. The remaining ~60-130us per call is therefore host-side launch-path work, not data movement, which is consistent with the frozen round-1 hypothesis and with the round-2 gain (-35 to -49us on this class): the launcher cache removed part but not all of the overhead. The same 67-81us latency band holds for the unprofiled members of this class (::0/::1 of all three dtypes), so the regime inference extends to all 12 non-::4 timing workloads, although it is measured only for the three profiled ones.

findings.label: ::4 shapes are already device/HBM-bandwidth bound at ~1.0 speedup (MTE2 read pipe critical)
findings.backend_detail: Ascend msprof op_summary pipeline ratios for the AI_VECTOR_CORE task; effective bandwidth computed as 2 x output bytes / avg duration and therefore an upper bound (100 invocations, single stream).

steady-state Task Wait Time between consecutive persistent-kernel tasks (float32 ::4): 0.0-0.2us, i.e. device fully back-to-back

findings.inference: The ::4 workloads move 512x65536 elements (33.55M) per way: 134.2MB total for fp16 (91.9us -> ~1.46TB/s) and 268.4MB total for fp32 (212.8us -> ~1.26TB/s). Authoritative eval latency (0.08875ms fp16; 0.21361ms fp32) matches the device duration, and the profiled Task Wait Time is ~0us, so these calls are fully device-bound and the host launch path is hidden. MTE2 (load) is the busiest pipe (0.92 fp16, 0.97 fp32) with MTE3 (store) at 0.79/0.82, so the load stream limits throughput; fp16 reaches ~16% higher effective bandwidth than fp32 on identical element counts and grids, hinting at modest headroom for the wider dtypes rather than a structural fix. Their ~1.0 speedup indicates torch's reference copy is limited by the same HBM bandwidth.

findings.label: At these sizes even the device portion is dominated by kernel start-up/scalar work, not data movement

findings.inference: The tiny/small kernels spend 0.41-0.49 of their AIV time in the scalar pipe with MTE2 ratios of only 0.21-0.23, and their per-invocation duration alternates between ~1.0-1.7us and ~3.0-3.6us, i.e. variation consistent with kernel dispatch/teardown jitter rather than data volume. Consequence: micro-optimising the device code for the non-::4 shapes cannot move walltime, because the kernel is already both negligible (1.4-2.6us) and start-up dominated; the only useful lever for those 12 workloads is the host-side per-call path.

performance_interpretation: Round 2 improved geo_mean from 0.3396 to 0.4708 (+38.6%) with no correctness regression; the per-workload deltas (-20.7% to -41.7% latency on 11 of 15 timing workloads, unchanged on the three ::4 controls) are consistent with the planned removal of per-call Triton launch-path work and therefore support the frozen hypothesis, which predicted 25-30us and delivered ~35-49us on several shapes. Profiling shows the hypothesis is only partially exploited: for the 12 non-::4 workloads the device kernel accounts for 1.4-7.7us of 66.8-133.3us walltime, so roughly 60-130us per call is still host-side and the class remains launch-bound. The three ::4 workloads are a separate, already-healthy regime: device time equals eval latency and MTE2 is 0.92-0.97 busy at ~1.26-1.46TB/s, giving ~1.0 speedup with little structural headroom. Overall bound is therefore mixed: host launch path for 12/15 workloads, HBM/MTE2 for 3/15.

next_experiment.action_description: Extend the round-2 per-signature launcher cache into a full steady-state fast path for the unchanged copy kernels: on the first call of a signature, capture not only the compiled launcher but also the final grid tuple, all constexpr values and a bound argument-marshalling closure; on subsequent hits, invoke that closure directly with only the fresh tensor/stream handles, without rebuilding the composite cache key (dtype, shape, every runtime integer, alignment), without re-reading the Triton JIT per-device cache and without re-deriving tile/grid selection. Key the fast path on a minimal precomputed signature (dtype pair + narrow offsets/extents) and keep the alignment/pointer fields out of the hot key (validate them once at insert time). Keep the existing kernel[grid](...) path as the fallback for any new or failing signature, and leave kernel bodies, grids and numerics untouched.
next_experiment.expected_impact: The 12 non-::4 workloads sit at 66.8-133.3us walltime with only 1.4-7.7us of device work; removing another ~20-30us of per-call host work would cut their latencies by roughly 30-45% and raise their speedups (now 0.29-0.57) proportionally, lifting geo_mean from 0.4708 into the 0.55-0.65 band while leaving the three ::4 device-bound workloads at their current ~1.0 parity.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: Risk: a key that omits pointer-alignment/dtype detail could serve a launcher specialised for an incompatible signature and produce wrong results or a launch failure; mitigate by validating the full signature once per new key and falling back to the generic path on any mismatch or exception, and by keeping correctness gating over all 18 correctness workloads. Risk: a captured closure must still receive the current tensors/stream per call so no stale handles are used. Rollback: revert to the round-2 candidate source (solution_sha256 cebeb6f587daa6f17be4882d7bca66ba500bcd7537f70c236fb5d85a9686d6f8) if geo_mean or any correctness workload regresses.
success_criteria: All 18 correctness-phase workloads remain PASSED with unchanged max abs/rel error.

geo_mean increases beyond the round-2 value 0.4708 (target >= 0.55), driven by further latency reduction on the non-::4 workloads (e.g. float16::0 below 133.3us, float16::2 and float16::3 below 68.4us).
The three ::4 workloads retain speedup >= 1.0 (no regression from the current 1.012 / 1.024 / 1.011).
No device-side regression: measured kernel durations for the fast-path calls stay within the 1.4-7.7us band already observed for the non-::4 shapes.

warnings: msprof and simulator timing is diagnostic and is not eval latency (service-reported).

Profiled launch cadence (92-109us) is larger than the authoritative eval latency for the same workloads (66.8-133.3us), so msprof-instrumented host gaps overstate per-call host cost; eval latency remains the basis for all comparisons.
Profile artifacts were collected for 5 of the 15 timing workloads; the remaining 10 were not profiled and are characterised only by analogy within their regime.
open_questions: The service exposes only metrics and instruction levels (no source-level mapping), so the remaining ~45-90us of per-call host time cannot be attributed to specific Python statements from profiler artifacts alone; a Coder-side host timing breakdown (perf_counter around cache lookup / argument marshalling / wrapper prologue) or an instruction-level request is needed to localise it.

Profiled launch cadence (92-109us) exceeds the authoritative eval latency for the same workload (66.8-133.3us), indicating msprof instrumentation inflates host-side spacing; profiler-derived host gaps are therefore directional only.

It is not yet established how much of the residual per-call cost is inside the reused launcher call itself versus the FlagGems/Torch op prologue (view construction, dtype/shape checks, dispatch); both are consistent with the current evidence.
Whether the fp16/fp32 effective-bandwidth gap on ::4 (1.46 vs 1.26TB/s) is recoverable on the device or is a dtype-dependent AIV load-path property is unresolved without instruction-level evidence.
